dedupe_keys.name: laparoscopic scissors hybrid discrete event and agent based simulation of a circular healthcare supply chain

description: This case study uses simulation to assess what happens across a healthcare supply chain when hospitals switch to circular medical devices, taking laparoscopic scissors as the example. The authors combined discrete event simulation of product flows with agent-based simulation of supply chain actors, such as manufacturers, hospitals and reprocessors, to capture interdependencies and variability, and posted the work as a preprint, free to read online on arXiv. Coverage is one product supply chain. Caveats: the preprint has not been peer reviewed, the case is one device type, and input data and parameters are not published with it. The study reports that it is the first to assess circular medical device designs at both member and system level; adopting circular products can reduce environmental impact, but significant reductions in both cost and emissions require substantial upfront investment; the model can also inform hospital inventory strategies that protect patient safety and operations. Simulation uses: a hybrid simulation template for healthcare supply chains and hospital inventory under circular economy transitions. Related records: the Queensland ward-level simulation (case_study-queensland-hospitals-ward-level-des-access-block) is another hospital discrete event simulation.
